headline: Best week in six years for Sensex and Nifty as Samvat 2082 bows out

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Saturday, the seventh of November, and this is your Market Brief. Diwali is tomorrow, so a very festive good morning to you.

Three things matter today. First, Indian shares just had their best week in nearly six years. The Nifty closed above 25,000 on Friday, even as a selloff in artificial intelligence stocks rattled markets from Seoul to New York.

Second, oil is falling hard. Brent crude is headed for a drop of about 16 percent this week, its steepest since 2020, on hopes that the war involving Iran may de-escalate. That helped lift the rupee to a six-month high.

And third, the tax on your equity gains is back in debate. The finance minister says she will consider investors' concerns, and a relief package is being examined, though an announcement before the Budget looks unlikely.

One date for your calendar: the Muhurat trading session is tomorrow, Sunday, from 2:20 to 3:30 in the afternoon.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Let's begin with how markets closed. On Friday, Dhanteras, the Nifty finished above the 25,000 mark, and the Sensex was up close to one percent through the afternoon. The Nifty has now rallied more than 10 percent in just seven sessions, and both indices posted their biggest weekly gains in nearly six years.

Business Standard calls it the anti-AI trade. With the global selloff hitting chip makers, cheaper oil and better earnings prospects have made India look attractive next to its Asian peers.

Within the market, pharma was the star. Aurobindo, Divi's and Glenmark hit new highs, and Symbiotec Pharmalab jumped 20 percent on results and an order win. Yes Bank rose 6 percent on Friday and 14 percent for the week. On the other side, capital goods had a rough day. The BSE Capital Goods index fell more than 3 percent, with Thermax, Apar and Astral down as much as 20 percent.

Now a look back at the whole Samvat year that ends with Diwali. Despite this late rally, Samvat 2082 was the weakest in fifteen years. The Sensex lost about 4 percent and the Nifty about 3 percent. Foreign institutional investors sold a record 4.55 lakh crore rupees of Indian shares over the year. But domestic institutions bought a record 8.55 lakh crore rupees, more than making up for it.

The levels to watch. Analysts quoted by Moneycontrol see the Nifty's immediate hurdle at 25,150, then 25,500. Support has moved up to 24,800, then 24,600. For the Bank Nifty, they are eyeing 59,500. And remember, after Sunday's Muhurat session, markets are shut on Tuesday, the tenth, for Diwali Balipratipada.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
Now to IPOs and deals. Samvat 2082 was the best year ever for the primary market. Companies raised a record 2.23 lakh crore rupees through 375 IPOs, up nearly 20 percent on the year before.

The pipeline stays full. The Securities and Exchange Board of India has cleared four more issues: Sagar Defence Engineering, Encube Ethicals, Arjun Jewellers and IFL Finance. Encube, backed by Quadria Capital, plans a 3,000 crore rupee issue, all of it an offer for sale. Coal India's subsidiary Mahanadi Coalfields also has the regulator's nod, for an issue that will be entirely an offer for sale by its parent. And Travomint's parent, SNVA Traveltech, has filed its updated draft papers for an issue of 12.75 crore shares.

In small-company listings, Maxwell Engineering Solutions debuted at a 90 percent premium, while Vectras Enprocon had a tepid start.

On deals, SoftBank sold Lenskart shares worth 1,896 crore rupees through block deals, bought by thirteen institutional investors at about 697 rupees each. Peak XV Partners and YC Holdings sold Groww shares worth 2,457 crore rupees, and Groww fell almost 4 percent. And V2 Retail rose seven and a half percent, even as its promoters sold 258 crore rupees of shares.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
On to the results roundup.

In engineering, Siemens reported a profit of 504 crore rupees for the September quarter, up about 5 percent. Revenue rose to 5,734 crore rupees, and new orders jumped 38 percent to 6,228 crore rupees. Bosch posted a standalone profit up nearly 22 percent, on revenue growth of 28 and a half percent. It also announced a one-for-five stock split and a three-for-one bonus issue, though the stock slipped 4 percent from the day's high.

In consumer goods, TTK Prestige grew profit 65 percent to 104 crore rupees, and its shares climbed 14 percent.

In construction, Hindustan Construction Company saw profit fall 53 percent to 22 crore rupees, though it did win an order worth 524 crore rupees. And in steel, BMW Industries grew profit 43 percent to around 22 crore rupees, as its new complex at Bokaro began operations.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
Now the economy. The rupee had a strong Friday. It rose 0.6 percent to close at 93.91 to the dollar, its best level since late April, helped by falling oil and foreign inflows. Over the Samvat year, though, it lost about 6.4 percent, and the 10-year bond yield rose 69 basis points.

Inflation is the worry. A Reuters poll of economists expects October's consumer inflation to come close to the top of the Reserve Bank's target band, driven by food, with food inflation seen around 8.2 percent. The poll says a rate hike is likely at the central bank's next policy meeting. Both the October inflation numbers and the minutes of the last policy meeting are due in the coming week.

The farm picture adds to that concern. Rabi sowing is down 46 percent from last year, at 37.6 lakh hectares, after a 48 percent rainfall shortfall in October. Sugar is the bright spot. Output has reached about 12.85 lakh tonnes so far this season, against just 3.2 lakh tonnes a year ago.

On activity, e-way bills hit a record 156 million in October, up 23 percent, pointing to strong festive demand. And Crisil expects states' capital spending to rise 10 to 12 percent this financial year, to about 8.5 lakh crore rupees.

Now to tax. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman says she will consider investors' concerns on equity taxation. Moneycontrol reports the government is examining a relief package, including changes to the securities transaction tax and a three-year holding period for long-term gains, but not before the Budget. Industry body FICCI wants the long-term capital gains tax on listed shares removed, offset by a higher transaction tax. And SBI Research has suggested no tax on gains held beyond three years, putting the cost at 40,000 to 50,000 crore rupees.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, it was a week of whiplash. On Thursday, the Nasdaq 100 suffered its worst day since the Covid crash, on worries over artificial intelligence spending, and Nvidia fell more than 9 percent. Friday brought a rebound. Chip stocks rallied over 4 percent, Nvidia gained 7 percent, the Nasdaq rose about 1 percent and the S&P 500 a third of a percent, while the Dow slipped about half a percent. Still, the S&P 500 had its biggest weekly drop since 2025, and the Nasdaq its fourth weekly fall in a row.

Asia took the brunt. South Korea's Kospi and Japan's Nikkei each fell around 6 percent, and Taiwan will curb short selling from Monday, the ninth.

US jobs data came in stronger than expected, with unemployment falling. That has raised bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike in December, and pushed gold lower.

And oil. Brent is on course for a weekly fall of about 16 percent, on hopes of de-escalation in the US-Israeli war on Iran, even as tanker attacks continue. For an oil importer like India, that is welcome relief, after Brent rose about 60 percent over the Samvat year.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Finally, your money. Gold and silver turned lower on Dhanteras. On the futures market, gold fell around 1,700 rupees to about 1,42,900 rupees per 10 grams, and silver slipped to about 1,84,800 rupees a kilo. If you are buying jewellery this festive season, check the hallmark's six-digit identification number, and verify it on the BIS Care app.

A warning for anyone who buys US stocks through an Indian platform. Bengaluru police have begun a probe into alleged unauthorised access to accounts at Stockal. Its parent, Borderless, says 13 investors lost about 6.26 million dollars, roughly 59 crore rupees, while Mint reports losses of over 100 crore rupees across nearly 30 investors.

The market regulator is discussing a rule to treat demat accounts as dormant after two years of inactivity. Around three-quarters of India's 24 crore demat accounts are estimated to be inactive, and the concern is misuse as mule accounts. Separately, the regulator has cautioned Dabur India over a delay in disclosing a warning letter from the US drug regulator.

In broking, Angel One has overtaken Zerodha as the second-largest broker by active clients, with about 7 million, behind Groww at nearly 14 million. If you trade in Sunday's Muhurat session, Zerodha says it will reverse brokerage on those trades.

On loans, the Reserve Bank's new norms from 2027 bar recovery agents from calling your colleagues or relatives. And state employees in Karnataka get a dearness allowance hike of 2.5 points, to 18 percent.

That's your brief. What to watch: the Muhurat session tomorrow afternoon, whether the Nifty can hold above 25,000, oil prices as the Iran situation evolves, and next week's inflation data and policy minutes. Happy Diwali, and have a lovely weekend.
